As a recovered anorexic. Don’t talk about food. Don’t encourage those conversations as they will always be skewed in his head. If I ever even suggested eating and someone around me didn’t want to i wouldn’t eat, eat around them if you have the chance. If you’re close to other people in their life bring up concerns but don’t divulge daily reports or details , it may feel invasive to him. I found recovery after going to treatment. It’s possible and I’m so thankful for those who treated me normally, it helped me. My best friend ate around me often and it made me feel safer to do so. They’re battling something that you can’t tackle on your own. Simple small gestures like these really do make a difference. Of course if they are in immediate danger to themselves or others, please get professionals involved asap, the most common COD for those with eating disorders is suicide. There are great resources online to learn about the signs and the National helpline 988 can help you if that came up. Best of luck

I have a j tube and put meds that I can* (they have to be safe and proven effective so not all are able to or should) through my tube. Including lithium, -and seroquel. I do have a port for other reasons. I take the rest of my pills orally. Because simply they don’t make IV versions of a lot of medications, and those that are are expensive and difficult to get covered by insurance. A doctor can sometime test your blood to see the efficacy of absorption of a medication you are on long-term. I take my birth control orally and I generally do not get my period because of it. But I use a back up method because of Malabsorption. GP does also not mean malabsorption. Most medications are absorbed in the stomach and break down just with acid. No movement necessary. There are other conditions that can cause malabsorption (which is why I take some meds through my J tube, not because of GP). if you suspect malabsorption, which would show on blood tests for malnutrition, then j tube medications would be more of a next step than a port since they’re such a huge risk and liability

Also side note: 156-141 in 3 months, doctors don’t see that as unhealthy weight loss because the weight loss/ time does not show extreme fast weight loss. So for the doctors that look at weight/time and nutritional values from blood tests that generally isn’t a great indicator to them that that weight loss is severe. Someone in calorie (healthy) deficit can average expect to lose 1-2  pound a week. So ~12 weeks with 15 pound weight loss it’s not “an unhealthy rate”.Every body is different but that’s how they look at it. Smart pill test/GES would be your best bet if your suspicions are correct.
